requirements.requirement: At least 512 MB of compressed in-memory swap configured on node1
requirements.summary: Baseline showed 0B swap (cmd-16be06c18f5d41e1). zram-generator installed and zram0 configured; after a stale-state reset, swapon --show and disksize confirm /dev/zram0 with 981M (1,028,653,056 bytes), well above the 512MB minimum, using zstd compression (cmd-eaec9fab824e496c, cmd-ae61c94869c04d36, cmd-137e2a8dd6f74b07).

requirements.requirement: Swap is compressed in-memory (zstd), not disk-backed
requirements.summary: /sys/block/zram0/comp_algorithm shows 'lzo lzo-rle [zstd]' indicating zstd is the active algorithm after the device was reset and restarted; confirmed again identically post-restart. No disk swap entries exist in /etc/fstab.

requirements.requirement: zram swap preferred over any disk-backed swap
requirements.summary: swapon --show reports PRIO=100 for /dev/zram0, well above the default -2 priority typical of disk swap. /etc/fstab has no swap entries at all, confirmed both pre- and post-restart, so zram is the sole and preferred swap source.

requirements.requirement: Swap is active at boot (persists across restart) with no manual intervention
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured (boot_id 4a743885..., zram0 981M, zstd, prio 100). A genuine reboot was issued (cmd-c205ff7d1d22488c) and connectivity loss observed (cmd-96d42365ca0c46d9), followed by reconnection with a new boot_id 91329670... (cmd-8d320f594fba4ac8). Post-restart verification shows /dev/zram0 automatically active with identical size, zstd compression, and priority 100, with the systemd unit active and no fstab disk swap — demonstrating the full healthy-baseline/disruption/recovery transition required for boot-persistence claims.

overall_summary: The executor fully satisfied the task contract: it installed and configured zram-generator on node1 to provide ~981MB of zstd-compressed in-memory swap at priority 100, with no disk-backed swap present, and directly demonstrated boot persistence through an actual reboot cycle (pre-restart baseline, disruption, boot-id change, and post-restart recovery showing the identical swap configuration active automatically). The independent node-restart evidence protocol cross-check (fixed after-prepare vs after-executor boot-identity snapshots) corroborates the same boot-id transition observed by the executor. Operational hygiene is high; the one non-trivial mutation beyond the core configuration (stopping/restarting the zram device to resolve a stale compression algorithm) was bounded, corrective, and directly contributed to satisfying the zstd requirement.
limitations: The after_prepare snapshot is an alias of before_prepare (prepare phase disabled), so it provides no independent preparer-state baseline distinct from before_prepare.
Only a single reboot cycle was captured; longer-term persistence across multiple reboots was not tested, though this is not required by the task.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands trace clearly to the task: package install and config write (cmd-eaec9fab824e496c) established the swap; the stop/reset/restart cycle (cmd-ae61c94869c04d36) was a bounded, low-risk corrective action to resolve a stale lzo-rle compression state left over from the initial start, directly enabling the zstd requirement to be met; the reboot (cmd-c205ff7d1d22488c) was the final bounded evidence-collection step required by the restart protocol and mirrored by the task's own boot-persistence requirement. No unnecessary mutations, abandoned files, failed services, or unsafe exposure were introduced. Lifecycle diffs (after_executor vs after_prepare) show only expected boot-identity-linked artifacts (new systemd-private tmp dirs, refreshed socket PIDs) with no residue attributable to careless executor action; failed-services list remained empty before and after.
